blocks.html_en: So what is the answer then? My best advice so far is that most things you do consist of two stages: doing and checking. You write some code, and you check it for bugs. You write some text and you fact-check it and proofread it.

sentences.en: So what is the answer then?
sentences.zh: 那么答案是什么呢？

sentences.en: My best advice so far is that most things you do consist of two stages: doing and checking.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我最好的建议是，你所做的大多数事情都包含两个阶段：执行和检查。

sentences.en: You write some code, and you check it for bugs.
sentences.zh: 您编写一些代码，然后检查它是否有错误。

sentences.en: You write some text and you fact-check it and proofread it.
sentences.zh: 你写了一些文字，然后对其进行事实检查并校对。

blocks.html_en: Current AI is not good enough to do both. It will work for a while, but eventually, there’s a real chance it goes off the rails. Sometimes in a big way, like deleting your database, but more often in more subtle ways, shifting the codebase slowly into an unmaintainable mess. More importantly, even if it does both flawlessly, can you really hand it in as “your work”? You have to ask what you are contributing. And, whether you’re a student or not, what you are learning.

sentences.en: Current AI is not good enough to do both.
sentences.zh: 目前的人工智能还不足以做到这两点。

sentences.en: It will work for a while, but eventually, there’s a real chance it goes off the rails.
sentences.zh: 它会工作一段时间，但最终，它很可能会脱轨。

sentences.en: Sometimes in a big way, like deleting your database, but more often in more subtle ways, shifting the codebase slowly into an unmaintainable mess.
sentences.zh: 有时会以很大的方式，例如删除数据库，但更常见的是以更微妙的方式，慢慢地将代码库变成无法维护的混乱。

sentences.en: More importantly, even if it does both flawlessly, can you really hand it in as “your work”?
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，即使两者都完美地完成，你真的能把它当作“你的作品”上交吗？

sentences.en: You have to ask what you are contributing.
sentences.zh: 你必须问你在贡献什么。

sentences.en: And, whether you’re a student or not, what you are learning.
sentences.zh: 而且，无论您是否是学生，您正在学习什么。

blocks.html_en: So, if you decide to use AI in some part of your project: let it do the thing while you check its work, or you do the thing, and it checks your work.

sentences.en: So, if you decide to use AI in some part of your project: let it do the thing while you check its work, or you do the thing, and it checks your work.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你决定在项目的某些部分使用人工智能：让它在你检查其工作的同时做这件事，或者你做这件事，它检查你的工作。

blocks.html_en: When you put the options like this, it’s really no choice at all. Having the AI write the code is what most people do. It’s what we call “vibe-coding”. If you hold to the above rule, you can only do this if you check everything the AI writes and does. It’s clear this is a fiction. The human brain was not made for this. Even if you resolve to really check, deeply, every line of code produced by the bot, your attention would wander in under an hour. The failure cases are rare enough that you can’t help but start to trust the machine.

sentences.en: When you put the options like this, it’s really no choice at all.
sentences.zh: 当你这样选择时，你真的别无选择。

sentences.en: Having the AI write the code is what most people do.
sentences.zh: 让人工智能编写代码是大多数人所做的。

sentences.en: It’s what we call “vibe-coding”.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们所说的“氛围编码”。

sentences.en: If you hold to the above rule, you can only do this if you check everything the AI writes and does.
sentences.zh: 如果你坚持上述规则，那么只有检查人工智能编写和执行的所有内容，你才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: It’s clear this is a fiction.
sentences.zh: 很明显这是虚构的。

sentences.en: The human brain was not made for this.
sentences.zh: 人脑不是为此而生的。

sentences.en: Even if you resolve to really check, deeply, every line of code produced by the bot, your attention would wander in under an hour.
sentences.zh: 即使您决定真正深入地检查机器人生成的每一行代码，您的注意力也会在不到一个小时内分散。

sentences.en: The failure cases are rare enough that you can’t help but start to trust the machine.
sentences.zh: 故障案例非常罕见，以至于您不得不开始信任这台机器。

blocks.html_en: More importantly, it wouldn’t be fun. Checking other people’s code is a grind. Writing your own is fun.

sentences.en: More importantly, it wouldn’t be fun.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，这不会很有趣。

sentences.en: Checking other people’s code is a grind.
sentences.zh: 检查别人的代码是一件苦差事。

sentences.en: Writing your own is fun.
sentences.zh: 自己写很有趣。

blocks.html_en: So let’s do it the other way around. You code and you have the AI check your work. Treat it like a reviewer. That’s my advice in a sentence. It can still save you time, it will catch bugs that would have taken weeks to figure out the old-fashioned way. It will tell you about tricks you missed and technology that you were unaware of. But, a lot of the incentives that point the wrong way in vibe-coding are turned around if you do it this way.

sentences.zh: 你编码，然后让人工智能检查你的工作。

sentences.en: Treat it like a reviewer.
sentences.zh: 像审稿人一样对待它。

sentences.en: That’s my advice in a sentence.
sentences.zh: 这是我对一句话的建议。

sentences.en: It can still save you time, it will catch bugs that would have taken weeks to figure out the old-fashioned way.
sentences.zh: 它仍然可以节省您的时间，它可以捕获错误，而如果采用老式方法，则需要花费数周的时间才能找出错误。

sentences.en: It will tell you about tricks you missed and technology that you were unaware of.
sentences.zh: 它会告诉您您错过的技巧和您不知道的技术。

sentences.en: But, a lot of the incentives that point the wrong way in vibe-coding are turned around if you do it this way.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你这样做的话，很多在振动编码中指向错误方向的激励措施都会被扭转。

sentences.zh: 在实践中你是如何做到这一点的？

blocks.html_en: Craft coding

sentences.en: Craft coding
sentences.zh: 工艺编码

blocks.html_en: Imagine three bakers. Hanna, Vivian and Cara.

sentences.en: Imagine three bakers.
sentences.zh: 想象一下三个面包师。

sentences.en: Hanna, Vivian and Cara.
sentences.zh: 汉娜、维维安和卡拉。

blocks.html_en: Hanna is a home baker. She’s fanatical: she goes to great lengths to let her sourdough starter mature, checking the temperature obsessively. She follows complicated rising processes: turning, retarding and shaping the dough very precisely. This leads to great bread, and she has more skill than many professional bakers. However, because she does everything by hand, including kneading the dough, it will never scale. She knows this, and she’s happy to create a few loaves of perfect bread in her own unique way.

sentences.en: Hanna is a home baker.
sentences.zh: 汉娜是一名家庭面包师。

sentences.en: She’s fanatical: she goes to great lengths to let her sourdough starter mature, checking the temperature obsessively.
sentences.zh: 她很狂热：她不遗余力地让酵母发酵剂成熟，并着迷地检查温度。

sentences.en: She follows complicated rising processes: turning, retarding and shaping the dough very precisely.
sentences.zh: 她遵循复杂的发酵过程：非常精确地翻转、延迟和塑造面团。

sentences.en: This leads to great bread, and she has more skill than many professional bakers.
sentences.zh: 这会带来美味的面包，而且她比许多专业面包师更有技巧。

sentences.en: However, because she does everything by hand, including kneading the dough, it will never scale.
sentences.zh: 然而，因为她所有的事情都是手工完成的，包括揉面团，所以它永远不会结垢。

sentences.en: She knows this, and she’s happy to create a few loaves of perfect bread in her own unique way.
sentences.zh: 她知道这一点，并且很高兴以自己独特的方式制作一些完美的面包。

blocks.html_en: Vivian is a commercial baker. Her bakery creates vast amounts of bread to fill the supermarket shelves. She defers most decisions about the baking process to food scientists she’s hired. She monitors aggregate statistics. Chief among them, how well the bread sells and how much it costs to make. She doesn’t care about the quality of the bread. Or rather, she cares about the quality to the extent that her customers care, but no more. She will happily use cheap flour to cut costs and reduce rising times to make production more robust. The main thing she’s worried about is getting undercut by another baker who figures out how to make bread that sells just as well, but a little bit cheaper. She’s not a bad person, she just cares about other things than Hanna, and if she didn’t, she wouldn’t last long in her job.

sentences.zh: 维维安是一名商业面包师。

blocks.html_en: In between these two extremes, we find Cara. Cara runs a commercial operation. She knows that she can’t bake bread the way Hanna does. No commercial bakery kneads dough by hand: it’s hugely inefficient and quite unhygienic.

blocks.html_en: However, Cara is not like Vivian either. She cares about the way the bread gets made. Good bread has intrinsic value to her. Even if her customers didn’t care, she still would. She’s on top of every part of the process, and this is what gives her satisfaction in her work.

blocks.html_en: Vivian is a vibe-coder. This is a little counter-intuitive, because “vibe-coding” suggests a kind of laissez-faire attitude where you don’t really care about the outcome and you’re just having fun. That’s what the phrase meant when it was coined, but the world has moved on. In many companies professional programmers are using AI in such a way that it’s impossible to imagine that they are also reading the resulting code in detail. This is what modern vibe-coding is. Deferring to the AI, not worrying about the individual lines of code, and keeping an eye on whether the code passes its tests and throws up any problems in production.

blocks.html_en: Cara is what we would call a craft baker, so the equivalent coding style could be called craft coding: a coding style that revolves around the inherent quality of the product, down to the details. Tools like AI are allowed, but only when they benefit that ideal, and only in a way that benefits that ideal.

blocks.html_en: One such niche, I believe, is scientific code. In science, the code is not normally the product. The thing we produce is an idea, captured in a paper. The code implements that idea, to prove it right. This means that scientific code has slightly different rules than production code. It doesn’t need to be robust to many different use-cases. It really only needs to run the experiments in the paper. That means that you can usually make it a lot simpler than production code.

sentences.zh: 我相信，这样的一个利基市场就是科学代码。

sentences.en: In science, the code is not normally the product.
sentences.zh: 在科学中，代码通常不是产品。

sentences.en: The thing we produce is an idea, captured in a paper.
sentences.zh: 我们产生的东西是一个想法，记录在论文中。

sentences.en: The code implements that idea, to prove it right.
sentences.zh: 代码实现了这个想法，并证明它是正确的。

sentences.en: This means that scientific code has slightly different rules than production code.
sentences.zh: 这意味着科学代码的规则与生产代码略有不同。

sentences.en: It doesn’t need to be robust to many different use-cases.
sentences.zh: 它不需要对许多不同的用例都具有鲁棒性。

sentences.en: It really only needs to run the experiments in the paper.
sentences.zh: 实际上只需要运行论文中的实验即可。

sentences.zh: 这意味着您通常可以使其比生产代码简单得多。

blocks.html_en: What’s more important than in production code, however, is that it’s correct. It absolutely needs to do exactly what the paper says it does. If your production code doesn’t quite do what you thought it did, but the customers don’t notice, it may not really matter. It’s not great, and you want your code to be correct, but if the incorrectness is harmless, you may get away with it. If it happens in science, it invalidates the paper.

sentences.en: What’s more important than in production code, however, is that it’s correct.

sentences.en: It absolutely needs to do exactly what the paper says it does.

Vibe-coding won’t get you there.

blocks.html_en: Until recently, my conclusion was that therefore, scientists should be hand-coders. Then, I started taking my own code and asking Claude whether it could spot any problems. So far, I have never shown it a snippet of code that it couldn’t spot a serious issue withg. The code usually runs, and I can’t see anything wrong with it. But the problems are there.

blocks.html_en: When I was a PhD student I wrote code by hand and I would eventually, in the course of my experiments, come across these bugs. I would get frustrated and spend weeks writing test suites to get rid of them. It took me years to develop that kind of discipline, and now that I am an assistant professor, with most of my time spent on teaching and various other non-coding activities, I’ve forgotten it. And if I did remember, I would conclude that I can no longer do serious research, because the code I write in the odd free afternoon is simply too full of bugs, even if it runs. The conclusion of my PhD was that the code for even a simple proof-of-concept experiment takes weeks of debugging, and even then, I’m not quite sure it really does what I think.

blocks.html_en: So, what does this craft coding look like in practice? Let’s separate the general philosophy from the main piece of advice I’m giving. Calling yourself a “craft coder” requires levels of self-importance that even I cannot rise to, but I may need a clear, simple phrase to summarize how a piece of code came to be. For that, we might use the more prosaic “Hand-written, AI reviewed” to summarize the key practice. “Craft coding” encompasses this but refers to the broader philosophy of (a) intrinsically valuing code quality and (b) accepting every tool that unambiguously brings you closer to that ideal.

sentences.en: So, what does this craft coding look like in practice?

blocks.html_en: The simple advice for now, given the state of current models, is not to let AI do anything. You only let it critique what you’ve done, and you implement its suggestions if you agree. The best metaphor, again, is that of a code review by a senior programmer.

blocks.html_en: You can do this however you like, but if you want some clear lines you should not let yourself cross, here are 10 dogmas of craft coding.

blocks.html_en: • Run the code to check for problems, then let the AI review find the rest.

sentences.en: Run the code to check for problems, then let the AI review find the rest.
sentences.zh: 运行代码来检查问题，然后让人工智能审查找到其余的问题。

blocks.html_en: • Don’t implement a suggestion you don’t understand.

sentences.en: Don’t implement a suggestion you don’t understand.
sentences.zh: 不要实施你不理解的建议。

blocks.html_en: I don’t follow all these religiously. My main sin, when I’m being lazy, or I’m too tired to think deeply, is to write sloppy code and to let Claude debug it for me without doing a pass myself.

sentences.en: I could out-code some of the early AI models, but that time is long past.
sentences.zh: 我可以对一些早期的人工智能模型进行编码，但那个时代早已过去了。

sentences.en: As a code reviewer, Claude Fable is definitely superhuman.
sentences.zh: 作为一名代码审查员，Claude Fable 绝对是超人。

sentences.en: It spots most mistakes without needing to run the code.
sentences.zh: 它无需运行代码即可发现大多数错误。

sentences.en: It spots many runtime bugs that I would never have caught myself.
sentences.zh: 它发现了许多我自己永远无法发现的运行时错误。

sentences.en: And it often has good suggestions.
sentences.zh: 而且它经常有好的建议。

blocks.html_en: It is required for security. This is a subset of the above point, but it bears highlighting. Humans do not write secure code. That was never a problem, because if we are not great at finding deep security problems, that cuts both ways, and the problems will, by and large, stay hidden. But a new entity has entered the chat. An entity that can very quickly find problems that we would never spot. You don’t have to agree that AI has greater intelligence, just that it’s different.

sentences.en: It is required for security.
sentences.zh: 这是安全所必需的。

sentences.en: This is a subset of the above point, but it bears highlighting.
sentences.zh: 这是上述观点的一个子集，但值得强调。

sentences.en: Humans do not write secure code.
sentences.zh: 人类不会编写安全的代码。

sentences.en: That was never a problem, because if we are not great at finding deep security problems, that cuts both ways, and the problems will, by and large, stay hidden.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是问题，因为如果我们不善于发现深层次的安全问题，那就是双向的，而且问题总体上会隐藏起来。

sentences.en: But a new entity has entered the chat.
sentences.zh: 但一个新的实体已经进入聊天室。

sentences.en: An entity that can very quickly find problems that we would never spot.
sentences.zh: 一个可以非常快速地发现我们永远不会发现的问题的实体。

sentences.en: You don’t have to agree that AI has greater intelligence, just that it’s different.
sentences.zh: 你不必同意人工智能具有更高的智能，只是它是不同的。

blocks.html_en: In recent months we have seen Mythos/Fable raise sufficient scurity concerns to make the US government step in. This release was followed by a wave of AI-assisted breaches and exploits. Then, last month, we found out that OpenAI and Anthropic’s models are actively circumventing their restraints [OpenAI, [Anthropic]((https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals)] in ways that their maintainers did not foresee.

sentences.en: In recent months we have seen Mythos/Fable raise sufficient scurity concerns to make the US government step in.
sentences.zh: 近几个月来，我们看到《神话/寓言》提出了足够的安全担忧，迫使美国政府介入。

sentences.en: This release was followed by a wave of AI-assisted breaches and exploits.
sentences.zh: 此版本发布后，出现了一波人工智能辅助的违规和漏洞利用浪潮。

sentences.en: Then, last month, we found out that OpenAI and Anthropic’s models are actively circumventing their restraints [OpenAI, [Anthropic]((https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals)] in ways that their maintainers did not foresee.
sentences.zh: 然后，上个月，我们发现 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的模型正在以维护者没有预见到的方式积极规避其限制 [OpenAI、[Anthropic]((https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals)]。

blocks.html_en: This means that in the age of AI, hand-written code is simply not safe. It will contain problems that we will never spot and that an AI-powered attacker can exploit effortlessly. Programmers need to loop AI in somewhere, somehow, or the game becomes laughably asymmetric.

sentences.en: This means that in the age of AI, hand-written code is simply not safe.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在人工智能时代，手写代码根本不安全。

sentences.en: It will contain problems that we will never spot and that an AI-powered attacker can exploit effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 它将包含我们永远不会发现的问题，而人工智能攻击者可以毫不费力地利用这些问题。

sentences.en: Programmers need to loop AI in somewhere, somehow, or the game becomes laughably asymmetric.
sentences.zh: 程序员需要以某种方式在某个地方循环人工智能，否则游戏就会变得可笑的不对称。

blocks.html_en: If you think you are special and different and you can write secure code every time, I beg you to let a modern AI model review it. Maybe I’m wrong in your case, and you can get in touch to gloat. I’m sure a few of you are good enough for that. I’m also sure it’s not the majority of you, and the majority of coders is where the majority of code comes from.

sentences.en: If you think you are special and different and you can write secure code every time, I beg you to let a modern AI model review it.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为自己很特别、与众不同，并且每次都可以编写安全的代码，我恳求你让现代人工智能模型对其进行审查。

sentences.en: Maybe I’m wrong in your case, and you can get in touch to gloat.
sentences.zh: 也许我对你的情况是错的，你可以联系我幸灾乐祸。

sentences.en: I’m sure a few of you are good enough for that.
sentences.zh: 我相信你们中的一些人足以胜任这一点。

sentences.en: I’m also sure it’s not the majority of you, and the majority of coders is where the majority of code comes from.
sentences.zh: 我也确信这不是你们中的大多数人，而是大多数代码来自大多数程序员。

blocks.html_en: Development speeds up. Again, compared to vibe-coding, craft-coding is still very slow. Compared to hand-coding, however, what you lose are those bugs that stop development in its tracks for weeks. The bugs that require whole new scripts and scaffolding to track down. For me, that’s still a meaningful saving. It means that with a few afternoons blocked per week I can still do meaningful work.

sentences.en: Development speeds up.
sentences.zh: 发展速度加快。

sentences.en: Again, compared to vibe-coding, craft-coding is still very slow.
sentences.zh: 同样，与振动编码相比，工艺编码仍然非常慢。

sentences.en: Compared to hand-coding, however, what you lose are those bugs that stop development in its tracks for weeks.
sentences.zh: 然而，与手工编码相比，您失去的是那些使开发停止数周的错误。

sentences.en: The bugs that require whole new scripts and scaffolding to track down.
sentences.zh: 需要全新脚本和脚手架来追踪的错误。

sentences.en: For me, that’s still a meaningful saving.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这仍然是一笔有意义的节省。

sentences.en: It means that with a few afternoons blocked per week I can still do meaningful work.
sentences.zh: 这意味着每周有几个下午的时间我仍然可以做有意义的工作。

blocks.html_en: It stops you from losing track of what your code does. For scientific code, this is really important. You need the whole codebase in your head. Every corner of it needs to be loaded into working memory. This is tough to do at the best of times. If you vibe-code, it is no longer possible. Little functions and classes will crop up without you knowing whether you asked for them and forgot, or whether the AI just inserted them at some point for some reason.

sentences.en: It stops you from losing track of what your code does.
sentences.zh: 它可以防止您忘记代码的用途。

sentences.en: For scientific code, this is really important.
sentences.zh: 对于科学代码来说，这非常重要。

sentences.en: You need the whole codebase in your head.
sentences.zh: 您需要将整个代码库记在脑子里。

sentences.en: Every corner of it needs to be loaded into working memory.
sentences.zh: 它的每个角落都需要加载到工作记忆中。

sentences.en: This is tough to do at the best of times.
sentences.zh: 即使在最好的情况下，这也很难做到。

sentences.en: If you vibe-code, it is no longer possible.
sentences.zh: 如果你用振动编码，那就不可能了。

sentences.en: Little functions and classes will crop up without you knowing whether you asked for them and forgot, or whether the AI just inserted them at some point for some reason.
sentences.zh: 小函数和类会突然出现，而你不知道是否是你要求了它们然后忘记了，或者人工智能是否只是出于某种原因在某个时候插入了它们。

blocks.html_en: It prevents (most) deskilling. Code reviews are not just good for the quality of the code. They are also an excellent way to transfer skills from a senior to a junior dev. It’s a really good teaching channel, because you’re talking about something that the junior has just written themselves. It’s all loaded up in their head and they can immediately understand anything you say about it. None of it will feel abstract.

sentences.en: It prevents (most) deskilling.
sentences.zh: 它可以防止（大多数）去技能化。

sentences.en: Code reviews are not just good for the quality of the code.
sentences.zh: 代码审查不仅有利于代码的质量。

sentences.en: They are also an excellent way to transfer skills from a senior to a junior dev.
sentences.zh: 它们也是将技能从高级开发人员传授给初级开发人员的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: It’s a really good teaching channel, because you’re talking about something that the junior has just written themselves.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的教学渠道，因为你正在谈论的是三年级学生自己写的东西。

sentences.en: It’s all loaded up in their head and they can immediately understand anything you say about it.
sentences.zh: 他们的脑子里全都充满了这些内容，他们可以立即理解你所说的任何内容。

sentences.en: None of it will feel abstract.
sentences.zh: 这些都不会让人觉得抽象。

blocks.html_en: With AI, you are the junior. The way things are going, you will always be the junior. That’s the bitter pill. There is no graduating to senior anymore, where you get to teach the young’uns how to code. All that’s left is to keep learning. However, the alternative is the Guitar Hero equivalent of coding: an infinitely fun game that makes you feel hugely powerful and creative, while removing all the difficulty and friction that cause you to actually learn anything.

sentences.en: With AI, you are the junior.
sentences.zh: 有了人工智能，你就是初级者。

sentences.en: The way things are going, you will always be the junior.
sentences.zh: 事情发展下去，你永远是小辈。

sentences.en: That’s the bitter pill.
sentences.zh: 这就是苦果。

sentences.en: There is no graduating to senior anymore, where you get to teach the young’uns how to code.
sentences.zh: 不再需要毕业到高级，你可以教年轻人如何编码。

sentences.en: All that’s left is to keep learning.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是继续学习。

sentences.en: However, the alternative is the Guitar Hero equivalent of coding: an infinitely fun game that makes you feel hugely powerful and creative, while removing all the difficulty and friction that cause you to actually learn anything.
sentences.zh: 然而，另一种选择是《吉他英雄》中的编码：一款无限有趣的游戏，让你感觉自己非常强大和富有创造力，同时消除了导致你真正学习任何东西的所有困难和摩擦。

blocks.html_en: With craft coding, not only do you prevent deskilling, you are actively learning. Like I said, the suggestions from Claude are usually genuinely good, and even if they aren’t, you are still judging for yourself whether to implement each one. Since everything filters through your active attention, you keep learning.

sentences.en: With craft coding, not only do you prevent deskilling, you are actively learning.
sentences.zh: 通过手工编码，您不仅可以防止去技能化，而且还可以积极学习。

sentences.en: Like I said, the suggestions from Claude are usually genuinely good, and even if they aren’t, you are still judging for yourself whether to implement each one.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，克劳德的建议通常都是非常好的，即使不是，你仍然要自己判断是否要实施每一条建议。

sentences.en: Since everything filters through your active attention, you keep learning.
sentences.zh: 由于一切都会通过你的积极关注而过滤，因此你会不断学习。

blocks.html_en: It limits environmental and financial impact. The environmental impact of AI is hotly discussed. The industry as a whole is having a worrying impact, and there is a real lack of transparency about energy use. For full-time vibe-coding, the costs are not negligible [2], and some companies are apparently finding that AI is more expensive than people.

sentences.en: It limits environmental and financial impact.
sentences.zh: 它限制了环境和财务影响。

sentences.en: The environmental impact of AI is hotly discussed.
sentences.zh: 人工智能对环境的影响受到热烈讨论。

sentences.en: The industry as a whole is having a worrying impact, and there is a real lack of transparency about energy use.
sentences.zh: 整个行业正在产生令人担忧的影响，而且能源使用确实缺乏透明度。

sentences.en: For full-time vibe-coding, the costs are not negligible [2], and some companies are apparently finding that AI is more expensive than people.
sentences.zh: 对于全职振动编码来说，成本不可忽略[2]，一些公司显然发现人工智能比人类更昂贵。

blocks.html_en: With craft coding this concern becomes minimal. A single, modest chat with Claude is enough for several days of coding. The basic $20/month plan pays for this and the environmental impact is less than that of the coffee you drink while coding [3].

sentences.en: With craft coding this concern becomes minimal.
sentences.zh: 通过手工编码，这种担忧变得最小。

sentences.en: A single, modest chat with Claude is enough for several days of coding.
sentences.zh: 与 Claude 进行一次简单的聊天就足以完成几天的编码工作。

sentences.en: The basic $20/month plan pays for this and the environmental impact is less than that of the coffee you drink while coding [3].
sentences.zh: 每月 20 美元的基本计划可以支付此费用，并且对环境的影响小于您在编码时喝的咖啡 [3]。

blocks.html_en: This is also something of a middle ground if you find it difficult to stomach giving AI companies your money. Right now, those $20/month subscriptions are not what’s keeping them afloat. If you want them to fail in some way, or to change their ways, but still want to understand the impact of frontier models on coding, this approach is at least better than burning tokens at the rate of full-time vibe-coders.

sentences.en: This is also something of a middle ground if you find it difficult to stomach giving AI companies your money.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现很难接受向人工智能公司提供资金，这也是一种中间立场。

sentences.en: Right now, those $20/month subscriptions are not what’s keeping them afloat.
sentences.zh: 目前，每月 20 美元的订阅费并不能维持他们的生存。

sentences.en: If you want them to fail in some way, or to change their ways, but still want to understand the impact of frontier models on coding, this approach is at least better than burning tokens at the rate of full-time vibe-coders.
sentences.zh: 如果你希望他们以某种方式失败，或者改变他们的方式，但仍然想了解前沿模型对编码的影响，这种方法至少比以全职振动编码员的速度燃烧代币要好。

blocks.html_en: It incentivizes checking your code. In most AI interaction patterns, the incentive is towards checking your own code less and less. Even if you don’t want to, a little laziness and a little time pressure is enough to defer to the machine a little bit more each day.

sentences.en: It incentivizes checking your code.
sentences.zh: 它会激励检查您的代码。

sentences.en: In most AI interaction patterns, the incentive is towards checking your own code less and less.
sentences.zh: 在大多数人工智能交互模式中，动机是越来越少地检查自己的代码。

sentences.en: Even if you don’t want to, a little laziness and a little time pressure is enough to defer to the machine a little bit more each day.
sentences.zh: 即使你不愿意，一点点懒惰和一点点时间压力也足以让你每天多一点点顺从机器。

blocks.html_en: It probably depends on your personality type, but when I treat Claude as my code reviewer, I find myself trying pretty hard to get the code bug-free before it looks at it (I never succeed). I know it doesn’t care, and there’s no one there to judge me. But that goes for the Duolingo owl too, and he still manipulates millions of people into practicing their Spanish every day.

sentences.en: It probably depends on your personality type, but when I treat Claude as my code reviewer, I find myself trying pretty hard to get the code bug-free before it looks at it (I never succeed).
sentences.zh: 这可能取决于你的性格类型，但是当我将克劳德视为我的代码审阅者时，我发现自己在查看代码之前非常努力地让代码没有错误（我从未成功）。

sentences.en: I know it doesn’t care, and there’s no one there to judge me.
sentences.zh: 我知道它不在乎，也没有人来评判我。

sentences.en: But that goes for the Duolingo owl too, and he still manipulates millions of people into practicing their Spanish every day.
sentences.zh: 但这也适用于 Duolingo 猫头鹰，他每天仍然操纵数百万人练习西班牙语。

blocks.html_en: So maybe it’s a little pathetic to want to impress Claude with my code, but if the alternative is apathy and deskilling, I’ll take it.

sentences.en: So maybe it’s a little pathetic to want to impress Claude with my code, but if the alternative is apathy and deskilling, I’ll take it.
sentences.zh: 因此，想要用我的代码给克劳德留下深刻印象可能有点可悲，但如果替代方案是冷漠和缺乏技能，我会接受它。

blocks.html_en: It stops you from self-delusions about being able to out-think the AI. It keeps you aligned with frontier AI abilities. Most of the people I interact with on social media are AI critics. On balance, I find them a healthier, more agreeable crowd than the Kool-Aid gang on Twitter. Still, being an AI researcher on Mastodon or Bluesky is not without frustrations. Not to put too fine a point on it, but most AI critics seem under-informed about how AI really works, and what frontier models can really do. Most criticism of the actual abilities is based on silly examples like the AI summaries above Google searches or the free version of ChatGPT from three years ago.

sentences.en: It stops you from self-delusions about being able to out-think the AI.
sentences.zh: 它可以让你不再自以为能够超越人工智能。

sentences.en: It keeps you aligned with frontier AI abilities.
sentences.zh: 它让您与前沿人工智能能力保持一致。

sentences.en: Most of the people I interact with on social media are AI critics.
sentences.zh: 我在社交媒体上互动的大多数人都是人工智能批评者。

sentences.en: On balance, I find them a healthier, more agreeable crowd than the Kool-Aid gang on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我发现他们比 Twitter 上的酷爱帮更健康、更友善。

sentences.en: Still, being an AI researcher on Mastodon or Bluesky is not without frustrations.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，作为 Mastodon 或 Bluesky 的人工智能研究员也并非没有挫折。

sentences.en: Not to put too fine a point on it, but most AI critics seem under-informed about how AI really works, and what frontier models can really do.
sentences.zh: 不想说得太过分，但大多数人工智能评论家似乎对人工智能的真正运作方式以及前沿模型真正能做什么了解不足。

sentences.en: Most criticism of the actual abilities is based on silly examples like the AI summaries above Google searches or the free version of ChatGPT from three years ago.
sentences.zh: 大多数对实际能力的批评都是基于愚蠢的例子，例如谷歌搜索上方的人工智能摘要或三年前的 ChatGPT 免费版本。

blocks.html_en: This makes some sense: if you’re fundamentally opposed to AI on moral grounds, you’re not going to shell out 20 bucks a month to Anthropic and keep up to date with all the latest developments. You’ll check in every now and then. It’s hard to blame people for that. But there are two serious problems with this approach.

sentences.en: This makes some sense: if you’re fundamentally opposed to AI on moral grounds, you’re not going to shell out 20 bucks a month to Anthropic and keep up to date with all the latest developments.
sentences.zh: 这是有道理的：如果你出于道德原因从根本上反对人工智能，你就不会每月向 Anthropic 支付 20 美元并了解所有最新进展。

sentences.en: You’ll check in every now and then.
sentences.zh: 您会时不时地查看一下。

sentences.en: It’s hard to blame people for that.
sentences.zh: 很难为此责怪人们。

sentences.en: But there are two serious problems with this approach.
sentences.zh: 但这种方法有两个严重的问题。

blocks.html_en: First, AI moves fast. To keep up with progress, you need to check carefully, every few months at least. Second, you have an ego-incentive not to check too carefully. Especially if you’re a hand-coder. Even if you’re very honest with yourself, there will be something in you that doesn’t want to know that a machine is outrunning you. If you’re not very disciplined, this something will stop you from checking quite as carefully as you would otherwise have done.

sentences.en: First, AI moves fast.
sentences.zh: 首先，人工智能发展迅速。

sentences.en: To keep up with progress, you need to check carefully, every few months at least.
sentences.zh: 为了跟上进度，您需要仔细检查，至少每隔几个月检查一次。

sentences.en: Second, you have an ego-incentive not to check too carefully.
sentences.zh: 其次，你有一种自我激励，不会检查得太仔细。

sentences.en: Especially if you’re a hand-coder.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你是一名手工编码员。

sentences.en: Even if you’re very honest with yourself, there will be something in you that doesn’t want to know that a machine is outrunning you.
sentences.zh: 即使你对自己非常诚实，你内心也会有一些东西不想知道机器跑得比你快。

sentences.en: If you’re not very disciplined, this something will stop you from checking quite as carefully as you would otherwise have done.
sentences.zh: 如果你不太自律，这会让你无法像平常那样仔细检查。

blocks.html_en: In this sense, craft coding keeps you honest. You still write your own code, one character at a time. It is still entirely yours, and you still understand every detail. But there is always that step of copy-pasting it into the Claude chat window and asking it if it can spot any problems.

sentences.en: In this sense, craft coding keeps you honest.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，手工编码让你保持诚实。

sentences.en: You still write your own code, one character at a time.
sentences.zh: 您仍然编写自己的代码，一次一个字符。

sentences.en: It is still entirely yours, and you still understand every detail.
sentences.zh: 它仍然完全属于你，你仍然了解每一个细节。

sentences.en: But there is always that step of copy-pasting it into the Claude chat window and asking it if it can spot any problems.
sentences.zh: 但总是有这样一个步骤：将其复制粘贴到 Claude 聊天窗口中，并询问它是否可以发现任何问题。

blocks.html_en: Ask yourself—if it really is just a parlor trick—why you don’t want to do that, at least every now and then?

sentences.en: Ask yourself—if it really is just a parlor trick—why you don’t want to do that, at least every now and then?
sentences.zh: 问问自己——如果这真的只是一个室内把戏——为什么你不想这样做，至少偶尔这样做？

blocks.html_en: What you still lose

sentences.en: What you still lose
sentences.zh: 你还失去了什么

blocks.html_en: The story is not all sunshine and roses. Deskilling is real, even if you use AI in a minimal fashion. What I learned to do in my PhD was to spend a week, 8 hours per day, debugging code. Even code I wasn’t sure had a bug. That was a whole skillset, it came with its own kind of creativity. It required persistence. With craft coding, that is mostly lost. If you have a deep bug, Claude Fable will just tell you. If AI ever disappeared for some reason, you would be shocked at the effort required to find these bugs yourself.

sentences.en: The story is not all sunshine and roses.
sentences.zh: 这个故事并不全是阳光和玫瑰。

sentences.en: Deskilling is real, even if you use AI in a minimal fashion.
sentences.zh: 即使你以最低限度的方式使用人工智能，去技能化也是真实存在的。

sentences.en: What I learned to do in my PhD was to spend a week, 8 hours per day, debugging code.
sentences.zh: 我在博士学位期间学到的就是花一周时间，每天 8 个小时来调试代码。

sentences.en: Even code I wasn’t sure had a bug.
sentences.zh: 即使是我不确定的代码也有错误。

sentences.en: That was a whole skillset, it came with its own kind of creativity.
sentences.zh: 这是一整套技能，它有自己的创造力。

sentences.en: It required persistence.
sentences.zh: 这需要坚持。

sentences.en: With craft coding, that is mostly lost.
sentences.zh: 如果采用手工编码，则大部分都会丢失。

sentences.en: If you have a deep bug, Claude Fable will just tell you.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个很深的错误，克劳德·寓言会告诉你。

sentences.en: If AI ever disappeared for some reason, you would be shocked at the effort required to find these bugs yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果人工智能由于某种原因消失了，你会对自己发现这些错误所需的努力感到震惊。

blocks.html_en: This is why I hedged above and said it prevents most deskilling. Note, however, that I didn’t say it reduces deskilling. It’s not about minimizing the harm. For the skills you still use, you will increase your skills, since the code reviews can show you things you didn’t know or didn’t think of. Only the skill of real deep, grinding debugging will probably fade. It’s not nothing, I’m sure there are many benefits to learning that process. But then many skills are lost as technology progresses. Maybe this is one we can afford to let go of.

sentences.en: This is why I hedged above and said it prevents most deskilling.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我在上面对冲并说它可以防止大多数去技能化。

sentences.en: Note, however, that I didn’t say it reduces deskilling.
sentences.zh: 但请注意，我并没有说它会减少去技能化。

sentences.en: It’s not about minimizing the harm.
sentences.zh: 这并不是为了尽量减少伤害。

sentences.en: For the skills you still use, you will increase your skills, since the code reviews can show you things you didn’t know or didn’t think of.
sentences.zh: 对于您仍在使用的技能，您将提高您的技能，因为代码审查可以向您展示您不知道或没有想到的事情。

sentences.en: Only the skill of real deep, grinding debugging will probably fade.
sentences.zh: 只有真正深入、磨练的调试技巧才可能会褪色。

sentences.en: It’s not nothing, I’m sure there are many benefits to learning that process.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么，我相信学习这个过程有很多好处。

sentences.en: But then many skills are lost as technology progresses.
sentences.zh: 但随着技术的进步，许多技能都消失了。

sentences.en: Maybe this is one we can afford to let go of.
sentences.zh: 也许这是我们可以放弃的。

blocks.html_en: What it won’t do

sentences.en: What it won’t do
sentences.zh: 它不会做什么

blocks.html_en: There are many things that craft coding won’t do for you. It won’t feel like magic. It won’t sick up that programming language you’ve been thinking about building for the past 10 years, at the cost of 6 hours of tokens. But maybe it’s time to accept that the world doesn’t need another programming language. Or if it does, that it also needs somebody to put in the time of maintaining and popularizing that language. And that goes for most of the things that you can magically vibe-code into existence. If you don’t have the time to maintain them and nurture them, you should keep them in your fantasies where they belong. The building time was never the bottleneck. The maintenance time is, and that is still a human job.

sentences.en: There are many things that craft coding won’t do for you.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情是手工编码无法为你做的。

sentences.en: It won’t feel like magic.
sentences.zh: 它不会感觉像魔法。

sentences.en: It won’t sick up that programming language you’ve been thinking about building for the past 10 years, at the cost of 6 hours of tokens.
sentences.zh: 它不会让您在过去 10 年里花费 6 小时的代币成本构建的编程语言感到厌烦。

sentences.en: But maybe it’s time to accept that the world doesn’t need another programming language.
sentences.zh: 但也许是时候接受这个世界不需要另一种编程语言了。

sentences.en: Or if it does, that it also needs somebody to put in the time of maintaining and popularizing that language.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果确实如此，也需要有人投入时间来维护和普及该语言。

sentences.en: And that goes for most of the things that you can magically vibe-code into existence.
sentences.zh: 这适用于大多数可以神奇地通过振动编码而存在的事物。

sentences.en: If you don’t have the time to maintain them and nurture them, you should keep them in your fantasies where they belong.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有时间维护和培养它们，你应该把它们留在你的幻想中。

sentences.en: The building time was never the bottleneck.
sentences.zh: 构建时间从来都不是瓶颈。

sentences.en: The maintenance time is, and that is still a human job.
sentences.zh: 维护时间是，这仍然是人类的工作。

blocks.html_en: If your company is doing the equivalent of selling bread to supermarkets, craft coding is going to be a hard sell. Mostly, companies won’t care about the inherent quality of code, or about how well their programmers understand every line of their codebase. They’ll care about the aggregate stats. Does it sell. Do the customers swallow it?

sentences.en: If your company is doing the equivalent of selling bread to supermarkets, craft coding is going to be a hard sell.
sentences.zh: 如果您的公司所做的相当于向超市销售面包，那么工艺编码将很难推销。

sentences.en: Mostly, companies won’t care about the inherent quality of code, or about how well their programmers understand every line of their codebase.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，公司不会关心代码的内在质量，也不关心程序员对代码库每一行的理解程度。

sentences.en: They’ll care about the aggregate stats.
sentences.zh: 他们会关心总体统计数据。

sentences.en: Does it sell.
sentences.zh: 有卖吗。

sentences.en: Do the customers swallow it?
sentences.zh: 顾客会吞吗？

blocks.html_en: But, just like Cara the craft baker finds her niche in people who are tired of the homogeneity of supermarket produce, so there is a niche for craft coding. I believe that scientific code, specifically the code that implements the experiments that we report on in our papers, should be craft coded. Not because AI is bad for you, and we should minimize its use. Not because science should be accelerated, and we must embrace AI for all it’s worth. But because if we use AI in the right way, the code will contain fewer mistakes, and the science will become more reliable. Everything else is of secondary concern.

sentences.en: But, just like Cara the craft baker finds her niche in people who are tired of the homogeneity of supermarket produce, so there is a niche for craft coding.
sentences.zh: 但是，就像卡拉一样，手工面包师在厌倦了超市产品同质化的人们中找到了自己的利基，因此手工编码也有其利基市场。

sentences.en: I believe that scientific code, specifically the code that implements the experiments that we report on in our papers, should be craft coded.
sentences.zh: 我认为科学代码，特别是实现我们在论文中报告的实验的代码，应该进行手工编码。

sentences.en: Not because AI is bad for you, and we should minimize its use.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为人工智能对你有害，我们应该尽量减少它的使用。

sentences.en: Not because science should be accelerated, and we must embrace AI for all it’s worth.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为科学应该加速发展，而是因为我们必须拥抱人工智能的全部价值。

sentences.en: But because if we use AI in the right way, the code will contain fewer mistakes, and the science will become more reliable.
sentences.zh: 但因为如果我们以正确的方式使用人工智能，代码中的错误就会更少，科学也会变得更加可靠。

sentences.en: Everything else is of secondary concern.
sentences.zh: 其他一切都是次要的。

blocks.html_en: The ethics of the thing

sentences.en: The ethics of the thing
sentences.zh: 事物的伦理

blocks.html_en: Well, almost everything. In science, the ethics of our methods should be of greater concern than the results they provide us with. If a result can only be obtained unethically, then we don’t obtain it.

sentences.en: Well, almost everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几乎一切。

sentences.en: In science, the ethics of our methods should be of greater concern than the results they provide us with.
sentences.zh: 在科学中，我们的方法的伦理问题应该比它们为我们提供的结果更受关注。

sentences.en: If a result can only be obtained unethically, then we don’t obtain it.
sentences.zh: 如果结果只能通过不道德的方式获得，那么我们就无法获得它。

blocks.html_en: For me, the conclusion so far is that I’m not happy with the way AI is built, but (a) I do see that it could be built better if we really wanted to and (b) a lot of the criticism, while not based on nothing, is being blown out of proportion. Those are strong claims, but I’ll have to substantiate them in a future essay.

sentences.en: For me, the conclusion so far is that I’m not happy with the way AI is built, but (a) I do see that it could be built better if we really wanted to and (b) a lot of the criticism, while not based on nothing, is being blown out of proportion.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，到目前为止的结论是，我对人工智能的构建方式并不满意，但是（a）我确实看到，如果我们真的愿意的话，它可以构建得更好；（b）很多批评虽然不是毫无根据的，但却被夸大了。

sentences.en: Those are strong claims, but I’ll have to substantiate them in a future essay.
sentences.zh: 这些都是强有力的主张，但我必须在以后的文章中证实它们。

blocks.html_en: For now, I’m putting AI in the category of things I can use reluctantly. I don’t fly or drive or eat meat, so that category is smaller than it may be for most people. It does include eating cheese, and having packages delivered to my door instead of to pickup points. It includes buying things from Amazon if they aren’t available elsewhere and it includes not deleting my Twitter account. Feel free to make your judgments. The point is we all decide to do some things we know are bad for one reason or another. Maybe because there are worse things, maybe because we think they are not inherently bad, just badly executed for the time being.

sentences.en: For now, I’m putting AI in the category of things I can use reluctantly.
sentences.zh: 目前，我将人工智能归为我勉强可以使用的事物类别。

sentences.en: I don’t fly or drive or eat meat, so that category is smaller than it may be for most people.
sentences.zh: 我不坐飞机、开车或吃肉，所以这个类别比大多数人可能要小的多。

sentences.en: It does include eating cheese, and having packages delivered to my door instead of to pickup points.
sentences.zh: 它确实包括吃奶酪，以及将包裹送到我家门口而不是取货点。

sentences.en: It includes buying things from Amazon if they aren’t available elsewhere and it includes not deleting my Twitter account.
sentences.zh: 它包括从亚马逊购买其他地方买不到的东西，也包括不删除我的 Twitter 帐户。

sentences.en: Feel free to make your judgments.
sentences.zh: 请随意做出判断。

sentences.en: The point is we all decide to do some things we know are bad for one reason or another.
sentences.zh: 关键是我们都决定因为某种原因做一些我们知道是不好的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe because there are worse things, maybe because we think they are not inherently bad, just badly executed for the time being.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为还有更糟糕的事情，也许是因为我们认为它们本质上并不是坏事，只是暂时执行得不好。

blocks.html_en: Beyond the current regime

sentences.en: Beyond the current regime
sentences.zh: 超越现行制度

blocks.html_en: Maybe these are all just temporary fixes. Maybe by the end of 2027, AI can do and check at the same time, for a long time, without any sudden failures and the above philosophy falls down. If that happens, however, there isn’t much that we can contribute anymore anyway. The need for programmers and scientists will drop by a factor of 10 or 100 or more, and it’s hard to predict what things will look like after that. Broadly, there are two options.

sentences.en: Maybe these are all just temporary fixes.
sentences.zh: 也许这些都只是临时修复。

sentences.en: Maybe by the end of 2027, AI can do and check at the same time, for a long time, without any sudden failures and the above philosophy falls down.
sentences.zh: 也许到 2027 年底，人工智能可以在很长一段时间内同时执行和检查，而不会出现任何突然的故障，上述理念就会崩溃。

sentences.en: If that happens, however, there isn’t much that we can contribute anymore anyway.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果发生这种情况，我们就无法再做出太多贡献了。

sentences.en: The need for programmers and scientists will drop by a factor of 10 or 100 or more, and it’s hard to predict what things will look like after that.
sentences.zh: 对程序员和科学家的需求将下降 10 倍、100 倍甚至更多，而且很难预测之后情况会是什么样子。

sentences.en: Broadly, there are two options.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，有两种选择。

blocks.html_en: First, no human cognitive skills will be required anymore, and we will defer to the machines in all aspects, with all the associated risks. If that is the case, we may as well invest in the skills and activities we enjoy, because working for our own entertainment will be all that’s left.

sentences.en: First, no human cognitive skills will be required anymore, and we will defer to the machines in all aspects, with all the associated risks.
sentences.zh: 首先，不再需要人类的认知技能，我们将在所有方面遵从机器，并承担所有相关的风险。

sentences.en: If that is the case, we may as well invest in the skills and activities we enjoy, because working for our own entertainment will be all that’s left.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，我们不妨投资于我们喜欢的技能和活动，因为剩下的就是为自己的娱乐而工作。

blocks.html_en: Second, some new set of skills will emerge. Something that people can do that machines can’t or won’t be trusted to. We don’t know what these skills will be. They could be creativity and long-term planning, but I wouldn’t bet the bank on it. In any case, we’re no good at teaching those, certainly not at universities.

sentences.en: Second, some new set of skills will emerge.
sentences.zh: 其次，一些新的技能将会出现。

sentences.en: Something that people can do that machines can’t or won’t be trusted to.
sentences.zh: 人们可以做而机器不能或不会信任的事情。

sentences.en: We don’t know what these skills will be.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这些技能是什么。

sentences.en: They could be creativity and long-term planning, but I wouldn’t bet the bank on it.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是创造力和长期规划，但我不会把赌注押在这上面。

sentences.en: In any case, we’re no good at teaching those, certainly not at universities.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们不擅长教授这些，尤其是在大学。

blocks.html_en: People often point to the calculator—I did so myself at the start—as something that came along and made a skill obsolete. The implicit conclusion being that when the calculator came along, kids were better off not learning mental arithmetic, because we were preparing them for a world that had calculators in it. But were they really? Even now, imagine two colleagues, largely similar but one is skilled at mental arithmetic and the other isn’t. Do you really think of the second one as having a useless skill, something like solving a Rubik’s cube: helpful to make you look smart, but otherwise pointless? Or does it actually come in handy, at least in technical professions: in helping you think through problems and analyse things on the hoof? The benefit may be smaller than before the calculator, but it’s not nothing.

sentences.en: People often point to the calculator—I did so myself at the start—as something that came along and made a skill obsolete.
sentences.zh: 人们经常指出计算器——我自己一开始就是这么做的——因为它的出现让一项技能变得过时。

sentences.en: The implicit conclusion being that when the calculator came along, kids were better off not learning mental arithmetic, because we were preparing them for a world that had calculators in it.
sentences.zh: 隐含的结论是，当计算器出现时，孩子们最好不要学习心算，因为我们正在为他们准备一个有计算器的世界。

sentences.en: But were they really?
sentences.zh: 但他们真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Even now, imagine two colleagues, largely similar but one is skilled at mental arithmetic and the other isn’t.
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，想象一下两位同事，他们基本上很相似，但其中一位擅长心算，而另一位则不然。

sentences.en: Do you really think of the second one as having a useless skill, something like solving a Rubik’s cube: helpful to make you look smart, but otherwise pointless?
sentences.zh: 你真的认为第二个技能是无用的技能，就像解决魔方一样：有助于让你看起来很聪明，但在其他方面毫无意义？

sentences.en: Or does it actually come in handy, at least in technical professions: in helping you think through problems and analyse things on the hoof?
sentences.zh: 或者它实际上是否派上用场，至少在技术职业中：帮助您思考问题并即时分析事物？

sentences.en: The benefit may be smaller than before the calculator, but it’s not nothing.
sentences.zh: 带来的好处可能比计算器之前要小一些，但也不是没有。

blocks.html_en: Similarly, when the ability to read and write code by hand becomes no longer strictly necessary, it might still be a useful skill to have. Something you don’t need for your job, but that can still set you apart. Something that can give you a deeper understanding of the job you’re hired to do.

sentences.en: Similarly, when the ability to read and write code by hand becomes no longer strictly necessary, it might still be a useful skill to have.
sentences.zh: 同样，当手动读写代码的能力不再是绝对必要的时，它可能仍然是一项有用的技能。

sentences.en: Something you don’t need for your job, but that can still set you apart.
sentences.zh: 一些你工作中不需要的东西，但仍然可以让你与众不同。

sentences.en: Something that can give you a deeper understanding of the job you’re hired to do.
sentences.zh: 可以让您更深入地了解您受聘从事的工作的东西。

blocks.html_en: Since we don’t know what skills will be fundamentally necessary, why not invest in those that give us joy, and those that have a decent probability of offering some benefit in the future, among whatever skills survive as AI improves.

sentences.en: Since we don’t know what skills will be fundamentally necessary, why not invest in those that give us joy, and those that have a decent probability of offering some benefit in the future, among whatever skills survive as AI improves.
sentences.zh: 既然我们不知道哪些技能从根本上来说是必要的，那么为什么不投资那些能给我们带来快乐的技能，以及那些在未来很有可能带来一些好处的技能，以及随着人工智能的改进而生存的技能。

blocks.html_en: Beyond that, I hope that this approach can help to create some center ground in a rapidly polarizing area.

sentences.en: Beyond that, I hope that this approach can help to create some center ground in a rapidly polarizing area.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我希望这种方法能够帮助在快速两极分化的地区创造一些中心基础。

blocks.html_en: In recent weeks:

sentences.en: In recent weeks:
sentences.zh: 最近几周：

blocks.html_en: • Codeberg [has come out strongly and broadly against AI coding]. The policy focuses mostly on vibe coding, but included in the type of projects that should consider themselves on borrowed time are “Projects heavily tied to the LLM ecosystem.” Moreover, the arguments given for the policy make it clear that this is not just about protecting their resources, but about pushing back against AI existing at all.

sentences.en: Codeberg [has come out strongly and broadly against AI coding].
sentences.zh: Codeberg [强烈而广泛地反对人工智能编码]。

sentences.en: The policy focuses mostly on vibe coding, but included in the type of projects that should consider themselves on borrowed time are “Projects heavily tied to the LLM ecosystem.”
sentences.zh: 该政策主要侧重于氛围编码，但应考虑借用时间的项目类型包括“与 LLM 生态系统密切相关的项目”。

sentences.en: Moreover, the arguments given for the policy make it clear that this is not just about protecting their resources, but about pushing back against AI existing at all.
sentences.zh: 此外，该政策的论据清楚地表明，这不仅仅是为了保护他们的资源，而是为了抵制现有的人工智能。

blocks.html_en: • Debian started a vote consisting initially of a Brexit-style choice between two extremes: disallow AI or embrace it. Happily, since then, the vote has expanded to include many options. One of them, option G, allows AI for review of human written coding, which aligns well with what I argued for above.

sentences.en: Debian started a vote consisting initially of a Brexit-style choice between two extremes: disallow AI or embrace it.
sentences.zh: Debian 发起了一次投票，最初包括在两个极端之间进行英国脱欧式的选择：禁止人工智能或拥抱人工智能。

sentences.en: Happily, since then, the vote has expanded to include many options.
sentences.zh: 令人高兴的是，从那时起，投票范围扩大到包括许多选项。

sentences.en: One of them, option G, allows AI for review of human written coding, which aligns well with what I argued for above.
sentences.zh: 其中之一，选项 G，允许人工智能审查人类编写的编码，这与我上面的观点非常一致。

blocks.html_en: • Linus Torvalds has come out in favor of allowing AI tools. The furore around this post made it look like he was arguing in favor of all AI coding, but the context of the discussion was about review tools. Elsewhere, he has stated that vibe coding is harmless so long as it’s not used for anything important. Interpolating between these positions, we can surmize that for kernel code, he’s probably a craft coder by the terms of this essay, while allowing a little extra elbow room for other people to make up their own mind. Note that the tool under discussion catches over 50% of bugs that human reviewers missed.

sentences.en: Linus Torvalds has come out in favor of allowing AI tools.
sentences.zh: Linus Torvalds 公开支持使用人工智能工具。

sentences.en: The furore around this post made it look like he was arguing in favor of all AI coding, but the context of the discussion was about review tools.
sentences.zh: 围绕这篇文章的愤怒让他看起来像是在主张所有人工智能编码，但讨论的背景是关于审查工具。

sentences.en: Elsewhere, he has stated that vibe coding is harmless so long as it’s not used for anything important.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方，他表示只要不用于任何重要的事情，振动编码就是无害的。

sentences.en: Interpolating between these positions, we can surmize that for kernel code, he’s probably a craft coder by the terms of this essay, while allowing a little extra elbow room for other people to make up their own mind.
sentences.zh: 在这些位置之间进行插值，我们可以推测，对于内核代码，根据本文的术语，他可能是一名熟练的编码员，同时为其他人提供了一些额外的自由空间来做出自己的决定。

sentences.en: Note that the tool under discussion catches over 50% of bugs that human reviewers missed.
sentences.zh: 请注意，所讨论的工具可以捕获人类审阅者错过的 50% 以上的错误。

blocks.html_en: In short, there is a heated discussion, with much polarization, but as ever the most important and productive steps are made in the center ground.

sentences.en: In short, there is a heated discussion, with much polarization, but as ever the most important and productive steps are made in the center ground.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这是一场激烈的讨论，存在很大的两极分化，但一如既往，最重要和最富有成效的步骤都是在中心立场上采取的。

blocks.html_en: The security issue makes the dilemma most clear to me. I no longer consider hand-coding a viable approach for safety-critical software. Not when we have access to a genuine super-human code reviewer who can instantly spot deep bugs that we may never have found otherwise.

sentences.en: The security issue makes the dilemma most clear to me.
sentences.zh: 安全问题让我最清楚地看到了这个困境。

sentences.en: I no longer consider hand-coding a viable approach for safety-critical software.
sentences.zh: 我不再认为手动编码是安全关键软件的可行方法。

content_html_zh:
这些天我们花了很多精力试图找出如何利用人工智能来阻止学生作弊。 这是必要的，但这并不是工作中最令人满意的部分。 想要学习捷径的学生无论如何都会找到它们。

一个更值得花费我们精力的有趣问题是如何告诉那些不寻找捷径的学生（包括博士生）。 那些真正想要学习并乐于每天投入数小时来发展自己的人。 那些想来这里的人。

这个问题——我们应该告诉学生如何使用人工智能——是一个很好的触发因素，让我们思考我们自己应该做什么（这就是这篇文章的真正目的）。

你最初的本能可能是告诉学生假装人工智能不存在。 以老式的方式学习一切。 从来没有对我造成任何伤害等等。 但这就像告诉 70 年代的学生假装计算器或计算机不存在一样。 今天的学生需要为人工智能将成为主要存在的世界做好准备。 他们需要具备驾驭这个世界的技能，无论它是什么样子。

或者，您可能认为我们应该告诉他们充分拥抱人工智能。 注册最高级别的克劳德并烧毁代币，就像没有明天一样。 绝对将一切交给机器。 这也是一个糟糕的建议。 这是绝对不会学到任何东西的可靠方法。

不仅如此，它还是确保你永远不会体验到学习某样东西的感觉的完美方式。 这一点并没有经常明确地表达出来：你在大学学到的最重要的事情之一就是衡量你是否真正理解一个想法。 你会发现自己处于一种情况，你可以发誓你真的理解了一些东西，然后你得到了正确的问题，但你不知道如何回答它。 最终，你学会问自己这些问题。 然后，慢慢地，你就会准确地感觉到自己是否真的达到了理解的状态。

将一切都交给人工智能意味着机器永远不会发展。 你不仅会故意走捷径，还会欺骗自己，让自己认为自己已经掌握了一些东西。 当账单到期时，你突然意识到自己根本没有任何有价值的技能，要解决问题可能为时已晚。

而且，这也适用于我们自己，即使我们很幸运能够在人工智能出现之前开发出这种机器。 认知技能就像肌肉：获得很难，失去却很容易。

那么答案是什么呢？ 到目前为止，我最好的建议是，你所做的大多数事情都包含两个阶段：执行和检查。 您编写一些代码，然后检查它是否有错误。 你写了一些文字，然后对其进行事实检查并校对。

目前的人工智能还不足以做到这两点。 它会工作一段时间，但最终，它很可能会脱轨。 有时会以很大的方式，例如删除数据库，但更常见的是以更微妙的方式，慢慢地将代码库变成无法维护的混乱。 更重要的是，即使两者都完美地完成，你真的能把它当作“你的作品”上交吗？ 你必须问你在贡献什么。 而且，无论您是否是学生，您正在学习什么。

因此，如果你决定在项目的某些部分使用人工智能：让它在你检查其工作的同时做这件事，或者你做这件事，它检查你的工作。

工艺编码

想象一下三个面包师。 汉娜、维维安和卡拉。

汉娜是一名家庭面包师。 她很狂热：她不遗余力地让酵母发酵剂成熟，并着迷地检查温度。 她遵循复杂的发酵过程：非常精确地翻转、延迟和塑造面团。 这会带来美味的面包，而且她比许多专业面包师更有技巧。 然而，因为她所有的事情都是手工完成的，包括揉面团，所以它永远不会结垢。 她知道这一点，并且很高兴以自己独特的方式制作一些完美的面包。

维维安是一名商业面包师。 她的面包店生产了大量的面包，摆满了超市的货架。 她将有关烘焙过程的大部分决定交给了她雇用的食品科学家。 她监控汇总统计数据。 其中最主要的是面包的销量以及制作成本。 她不关心面包的质量。 或者更确切地说，她关心质量就像她的客户关心的那样，但仅此而已。 她很乐意使用廉价面粉来降低成本并减少发酵时间，从而使生产更加强劲。 她最担心的是被另一位面包师削弱，这位面包师想出了如何制作出同样畅销但更便宜一点的面包。 她不是一个坏人，她只是关心汉娜以外的其他事情，如果她不关心，她的工作就不会长久。

在这两个极端之间，我们找到了卡拉。 卡拉经营一家商业公司。 她知道她无法像汉娜那样烤面包。 没有一家商业面包店会用手揉面团：效率极低，而且很不卫生。

然而，卡拉也不像薇薇安。 她关心面包的制作方式。 好面包对她来说具有内在价值。 即使她的顾客不关心，她仍然会关心。 她掌控整个流程的每个部分，这也是她对工作感到满意的原因。

这映射到现代编码实践如下。

Cara 是我们所说的工艺面包师，因此等效的编码风格可以称为工艺编码：一种围绕产品的内在质量，深入到细节的编码风格。 程序员致力于详细了解代码库的各个方面。 像人工智能这样的工具是被允许的，但前提是它们有利于实现这一理想，并且只能以有利于实现这一理想的方式。

工艺至关重要的地方

我相信，这样的一个利基市场就是科学代码。 在科学中，代码通常不是产品。 我们产生的东西是一个想法，记录在论文中。 代码实现了这个想法，并证明它是正确的。 这意味着科学代码的规则与生产代码略有不同。 它不需要对许多不同的用例都具有鲁棒性。 实际上只需要运行论文中的实验即可。 这意味着您通常可以使其比生产代码简单得多。

然而，比生产代码更重要的是它是正确的。 它绝对需要完全按照论文所说的去做。 如果您的生产代码并不完全符合您的预期，但客户没有注意到，那么这可能并不重要。 这不太好，你希望你的代码是正确的，但如果不正确是无害的，你可能会侥幸逃脱。 如果这种情况发生在科学领域，论文就会失效。

我可以写一篇关于这如何影响科学编码风格的整篇文章，但我们会留到下次再说。 目前，这意味着科学是工艺编码的一个强大利基。 作为论文的作者，您保证代码完全实现了论文的思想。 只有当您逐行熟悉代码时才能做到这一点。 氛围编码不会让你到达那里。

直到最近，我的结论是，因此，科学家应该是手工编码员。 然后，我开始使用自己的代码并询问 Claude 它是否可以发现任何问题。 到目前为止，我从未向它展示过它无法发现严重问题的代码片段。 代码通常可以运行，我看不出有什么问题。 但问题是存在的。

当我还是一名博士生时，我手工编写代码，最终在实验过程中遇到了这些错误。 我会感到沮丧并花费数周时间编写测试套件来摆脱它们。 我花了很多年的时间来发展这种学科，现在我是一名助理教授，大部分时间都花在教学和各种其他非编码活动上，我已经忘记了它。 如果我确实记得的话，我会得出这样的结论：我无法再进行认真的研究，因为我在空闲的下午编写的代码即使运行也充满了错误。 我的博士学位得出的结论是，即使是一个简单的概念验证实验的代码也需要数周的调试，即便如此，我也不太确定它是否真的按照我的想法进行。

这就是我们回到面包师的地方。 卡拉可能会为她的揉捏感到自豪。 她可能喜欢用手揉面团，因为这真的可以让你感受到面筋是如何形成的。 然而，如果她要经营商业业务，她需要接受一个简单的事实：使用揉捏机可以制作出更好的面团、更卫生的过程和更可预测的结果。 简而言之，如果该工具使产品变得更好，您就需要接受这一点。

这并不意味着您需要盲目或不加批判地接受它。 卡拉仍然可以决定她使用哪台捏合机以及如何使用它，但她至少应该接受机器可以比她做得更好的某些事情。

鉴于当前模型的状态，目前简单的建议是不要让人工智能做任何事情。 你只让它批评你所做的事情，如果你同意，你就实施它的建议。 最好的比喻还是由高级程序员进行的代码审查。

  1. IDE 中没有 AI。 其中包括 LLM 驱动的自动完成功能。 每行的每个字符都是通过用一根手指敲击键盘上的按键来书写的。

  5. 不要使用人工智能来做任何普通搜索可以做的事情。
  6. 在询问 AI 之前，请先阅读文档。
  7. 仅当您自己无法解决时才向人工智能寻求解决方案。 给自己一些时间思考。
  8. 在要求人工智能审查之前，请先检查一下您的代码。 尽最大努力减少错误。
  9. 运行代码来检查问题，然后让人工智能审查找到其余的问题。
  10. 不要实施你不理解的建议。

我并不虔诚地遵循所有这些。 当我懒惰或太累而无法深入思考时，我的主要罪过就是编写草率的代码并让克劳德为我调试它而不自己做一遍。

你还失去了什么

这个故事并不全是阳光和玫瑰。 即使你以最低限度的方式使用人工智能，去技能化也是真实存在的。 我在博士学位期间学到的就是花一周时间，每天 8 个小时来调试代码。 即使是我不确定的代码也有错误。 这是一整套技能，它有自己的创造力。 这需要坚持。 如果采用手工编码，则大部分都会丢失。 如果你有一个很深的错误，克劳德·寓言会告诉你。 如果人工智能由于某种原因消失了，你会对自己发现这些错误所需的努力感到震惊。

这就是为什么我在上面对冲并说它可以防止大多数去技能化。 但请注意，我并没有说它会减少去技能化。 这并不是为了尽量减少伤害。 对于您仍在使用的技能，您将提高您的技能，因为代码审查可以向您展示您不知道或没有想到的事情。 只有真正深入、磨练的调试技巧才可能会褪色。 这并不是什么，我相信学习这个过程有很多好处。 但随着技术的进步，许多技能都消失了。 也许这是我们可以放弃的。

它不会做什么

有很多事情是手工编码无法为你做的。 它不会感觉像魔法。 它不会让您在过去 10 年里花费 6 小时的代币成本构建的编程语言感到厌烦。 但也许是时候接受这个世界不需要另一种编程语言了。 或者，如果确实如此，也需要有人投入时间来维护和普及该语言。 这适用于大多数可以神奇地通过振动编码而存在的事物。 如果你没有时间维护和培养它们，你应该把它们留在你的幻想中。 构建时间从来都不是瓶颈。 维护时间是，这仍然是人类的工作。

如果您的公司所做的相当于向超市销售面包，那么工艺编码将很难推销。 大多数情况下，公司不会关心代码的内在质量，也不关心程序员对代码库每一行的理解程度。 他们会关心总体统计数据。 有卖吗。 顾客会吞吗？

但是，就像卡拉一样，手工面包师在厌倦了超市产品同质化的人们中找到了自己的利基，因此手工编码也有其利基市场。 我认为科学代码，特别是实现我们在论文中报告的实验的代码，应该进行手工编码。 并不是因为人工智能对你有害，我们应该尽量减少它的使用。 并不是因为科学应该加速发展，而是因为我们必须拥抱人工智能的全部价值。 但因为如果我们以正确的方式使用人工智能，代码中的错误就会更少，科学也会变得更加可靠。 其他一切都是次要的。

事物的伦理

嗯，几乎一切。 在科学中，我们的方法的伦理问题应该比它们为我们提供的结果更受关注。 如果结果只能通过不道德的方式获得，那么我们就无法获得它。

对我来说，到目前为止的结论是，我对人工智能的构建方式并不满意，但是（a）我确实看到，如果我们真的愿意的话，它可以构建得更好；（b）很多批评虽然不是毫无根据的，但却被夸大了。 这些都是强有力的主张，但我必须在以后的文章中证实它们。

目前，我将人工智能归为我勉强可以使用的事物类别。 我不坐飞机、开车或吃肉，所以这个类别比大多数人可能要小的多。 它确实包括吃奶酪，以及将包裹送到我家门口而不是取货点。 它包括从亚马逊购买其他地方买不到的东西，也包括不删除我的 Twitter 帐户。 请随意做出判断。 关键是我们都决定因为某种原因做一些我们知道是不好的事情。 也许是因为还有更糟糕的事情，也许是因为我们认为它们本质上并不是坏事，只是暂时执行得不好。

超越现行制度

也许这些都只是临时修复。 也许到 2027 年底，人工智能可以在很长一段时间内同时执行和检查，而不会出现任何突然的故障，上述理念就会崩溃。 然而，如果发生这种情况，我们就无法再做出太多贡献了。 对程序员和科学家的需求将下降 10 倍、100 倍甚至更多，而且很难预测之后情况会是什么样子。 一般来说，有两种选择。

首先，不再需要人类的认知技能，我们将在所有方面遵从机器，并承担所有相关的风险。 如果是这样的话，我们不妨投资于我们喜欢的技能和活动，因为剩下的就是为自己的娱乐而工作。

其次，一些新的技能将会出现。 人们可以做而机器不能或不会信任的事情。 我们不知道这些技能是什么。 它们可能是创造力和长期规划，但我不会把赌注押在这上面。 无论如何，我们不擅长教授这些，尤其是在大学。

人们经常指出计算器——我自己一开始就是这么做的——因为它的出现让一项技能变得过时。 隐含的结论是，当计算器出现时，孩子们最好不要学习心算，因为我们正在为他们准备一个有计算器的世界。 但他们真的是这样吗？ 即使是现在，想象一下两位同事，他们基本上很相似，但其中一位擅长心算，而另一位则不然。 你真的认为第二个技能是无用的技能，就像解决魔方一样：有助于让你看起来很聪明，但在其他方面毫无意义？ 或者它实际上是否派上用场，至少在技术职业中：帮助您思考问题并即时分析事物？ 带来的好处可能比计算器之前要小一些，但也不是没有。

同样，当手动读写代码的能力不再是绝对必要的时，它可能仍然是一项有用的技能。 一些你工作中不需要的东西，但仍然可以让你与众不同。 可以让您更深入地了解您受聘从事的工作的东西。

既然我们不知道哪些技能从根本上来说是必要的，那么为什么不投资那些能给我们带来快乐的技能，以及那些在未来很有可能带来一些好处的技能，以及随着人工智能的改进而生存的技能。

除此之外，我希望这种方法能够帮助在快速两极分化的地区创造一些中心基础。

最近几周：

  • Codeberg [强烈而广泛地反对人工智能编码]。 该政策主要侧重于氛围编码，但应考虑借用时间的项目类型包括“与 LLM 生态系统密切相关的项目”。 此外，该政策的论据清楚地表明，这不仅仅是为了保护他们的资源，而是为了抵制现有的人工智能。
  • Debian 发起了一次投票，最初包括在两个极端之间进行英国脱欧式的选择：禁止人工智能或拥抱人工智能。 令人高兴的是，从那时起，投票范围扩大到包括许多选项。 其中之一，选项 G，允许人工智能审查人类编写的编码，这与我上面的观点非常一致。
  • Linus Torvalds 公开支持使用人工智能工具。 围绕这篇文章的愤怒让他看起来像是在主张所有人工智能编码，但讨论的背景是关于审查工具。 在其他地方，他表示只要不用于任何重要的事情，振动编码就是无害的。 在这些位置之间进行插值，我们可以推测，对于内核代码，根据本文的术语，他可能是一名熟练的编码员，同时为其他人提供了一些额外的自由空间来做出自己的决定。 请注意，所讨论的工具可以捕获人类审阅者错过的 50% 以上的错误。

简而言之，这是一场激烈的讨论，存在很大的两极分化，但一如既往，最重要和最富有成效的步骤都是在中心立场上采取的。

安全问题让我最清楚地看到了这个困境。 我不再认为手动编码是安全关键软件的可行方法。 当我们能够接触到真正的超人代码审查员时，他可以立即发现我们可能永远无法发现的深层错误。

这并不意味着我们必须将一切交给人工智能。 这确实意味着我们必须仔细考虑我们的选择。 而且，稍微缩小一点，这意味着我们必须抵制对两极分化的永不满足的渴望。 这不是一个双边问题。 很少有问题。 这是一个伟大的中间立场，充满了聪明、有趣和令人兴奋的机会。 只要我们小心谨慎，不断动动脑筋，解决办法就在那里。

为了实践我所宣扬的，我“精心撰写”了这篇博文。 我写了并检查了初稿，然后请克劳德·法布尔校对它，进行事实核查并给我一个总体评论。 如果您愿意，可以在这里阅读原稿。

当然，它发现了许多错别字，还有一些英语习语的错误。 更有趣的是，它标记了一些夸大的评论，以及我应该真正证实的事情，这导致了下面的脚注。 这也许是构建任何东西时审查阶段的主要好处。 它迫使你想要完成的疲惫部分和想要发表的兴奋部分安静一段时间，并且它为你提供了一种方法来批判性地检查你最后一次完成的事情。 批评是什么并不重要，阅读批评的行为，在你的文本或代码中找到批评的目标，并思考你是否同意，就足以让你的工作再坚持一段时间。

克劳德最有帮助的一般性批评是，目标受众有点偏离，而我对受众的态度有点不公平（无论他们是氛围编码者还是人工智能怀疑论者）。 我修复了后一部分，并在开始时将流动的观众最小化。 但实际上，我有点喜欢散文中散漫的一面，所以我决定在这种情况下不要过多听克劳德的讲话。

与毛利润相比，研发成本为 190 亿美元，销售和营销成本为 56 亿美元，一般和管理成本为 16 亿美元。

换句话说，如果 OpenAI 取消所有研发（即解雇所有研究人员并且不再训练更多新模型），并将 S&M 削减约 20 亿美元，那么他们今天就会盈利。 似乎没有人知道 S&M 预算中有什么，但审计人员显然不太可能允许象征性补贴进入其中。

总而言之，我最好的猜测是，API 代币通常都是以盈利方式出售的，而免费和统一费率的代币则得到了大量补贴以占领市场份额，但大部分盈利能力差距实际上是培训新模型的前期费用和留住研究人才的成本。

我最近的一次为期两天的工艺编码会议导致了大约 1800 个单词的聊天（包括我的），所以最糟糕的是两天内消耗了大约 9 升水。 我每天喝大约3杯咖啡，所以咖啡的成本是33.6升。

接下来，我们可以看看能源的使用。 人工智能公司并不透明，他们因此受到的所有批评都是应得的。 然而，在我们的例子中，差异足够大，我们不需要准确的数字。 生产 100 毫升咖啡的成本显然约为半千瓦时。 大约一年前，Gemini 的 LLM 查询成本中位数约为四分之一瓦时。 因此，即使《神鬼寓言》的代码审查成本是这个成本的两倍，我们仍然比制作一小杯咖啡所需的能源低三个数量级。

我这里忽略了训练成本，只计算推理。 训练成本是一个模型在下一个模型取代它之前的使用程度的一个因素。 如果您愿意永远继续使用当前一代的模型，那么您就可以进行工艺编码，并且《神鬼寓言》的培训成本将在很长一段时间内摊销，以至于可以忽略不计。 如果你在最新的模型可用时就切换到它，并且 Anthropic 每年都不断训练一个新模型，那么能源消耗会增加，但与一杯咖啡相比，它仍然可以忽略不计。
